variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Machine learning is a way to build software that learns a useful pattern from examples. Instead of writing every decision rule by hand, a team defines what should be predicted, provides representative evidence, and trains a model to map inputs to an output.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Data
pairs.detail: Features describe each case.
pairs.explanation: Features describe each case. Labels or observed outcomes provide the signal the system should learn. Coverage and correctness set an upper bound on useful quality.

pairs.label: Model
pairs.detail: A parameterized function converts features into a value, category, score, ordering, or generated output.
pairs.explanation: A parameterized function converts features into a value, category, score, ordering, or generated output.

pairs.label: Training
pairs.detail: An optimization process compares predictions with an objective and adjusts parameters to reduce error on training examples.
pairs.explanation: An optimization process compares predictions with an objective and adjusts parameters to reduce error on training examples.

pairs.label: Inference
pairs.detail: The trained model processes a new input.
pairs.explanation: The trained model processes a new input. Product policy turns its output and uncertainty into an action.

variants.hint:
Data: Features describe each case.

Model: A parameterized function converts features into a value, category, score, ordering, or generated output.

Training: An optimization process compares predictions with an objective and adjusts parameters to reduce error on training examples.

Inference: The trained model processes a new input.

pairs.label: Supervised learning
pairs.detail: Learn from input-target pairs.
pairs.explanation: Learn from input-target pairs. Use it for outcomes such as delivery time, fraud status, demand, or relevance when trustworthy labels can be defined.

pairs.label: Unsupervised learning
pairs.detail: Find structure in inputs without one correct target per example.
pairs.explanation: Find structure in inputs without one correct target per example. Common goals include grouping similar cases, compressing representations, and finding unusual patterns.

pairs.label: Reinforcement learning
pairs.detail: Learn a policy from actions, outcomes, and delayed reward.
pairs.explanation: Learn a policy from actions, outcomes, and delayed reward. The action changes what happens next, so exploration and long-term consequences matter.

variants.hint:
Supervised learning: Learn from input-target pairs.

Unsupervised learning: Find structure in inputs without one correct target per example.

Reinforcement learning: Learn a policy from actions, outcomes, and delayed reward.

pairs.label: Build protected evidence
pairs.detail: Create training, validation, and test boundaries that prevent the same entity, future event, or duplicate example from leaking across splits.
pairs.explanation: Create training, validation, and test boundaries that prevent the same entity, future event, or duplicate example from leaking across splits.

pairs.label: Fit and compare
pairs.detail: Optimize on training data, use validation data for model decisions, and compare every candidate with a simple baseline.
pairs.explanation: Optimize on training data, use validation data for model decisions, and compare every candidate with a simple baseline.

pairs.label: Release with limits
pairs.detail: Evaluate important slices, latency, and failures; then use shadow or canary traffic before letting predictions control the full workflow.
pairs.explanation: Evaluate important slices, latency, and failures; then use shadow or canary traffic before letting predictions control the full workflow.

pairs.label: Underfitting
pairs.detail: Training and unseen quality are both weak.
pairs.explanation: Training and unseen quality are both weak. Improve signal, features, optimization, or capacity one controlled step at a time.

pairs.label: Overfitting
pairs.detail: Training quality is strong while unseen quality lags.
pairs.explanation: Training quality is strong while unseen quality lags. Try simpler capacity, regularization, early stopping, or more representative data.

pairs.label: Distribution shift
pairs.detail: The deployment population differs from the evaluation evidence.
pairs.explanation: The deployment population differs from the evaluation evidence. Report important slices and update the data boundary before trusting one aggregate metric.

variants.context: Machine learning is a way to build software that learns a useful pattern from examples. Instead of writing every decision rule by hand, a team defines what should be predicted, provides representative evidence, and trains a model to map inputs to an output.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Regression errors
pairs.detail: MAE gives each absolute error equal weight.
pairs.explanation: MAE gives each absolute error equal weight. RMSE emphasizes large errors. Report domain units and important slices so a good average cannot hide costly misses.

pairs.label: Classification errors
pairs.detail: Precision describes how often positive predictions are right; recall describes how many actual positives are found.
pairs.explanation: Precision describes how often positive predictions are right; recall describes how many actual positives are found. The decision threshold trades one mistake type against the other.

pairs.label: Ranking errors
pairs.detail: Metrics such as precision at K or NDCG emphasize the positions users actually inspect.
pairs.explanation: Metrics such as precision at K or NDCG emphasize the positions users actually inspect. Online outcomes still need guardrails against feedback loops and position bias.

pairs.label: Start with rules
pairs.detail: Use explicit logic when rules are stable, exact explanation is required, and the cases remain practical to maintain directly.
pairs.explanation: Use explicit logic when rules are stable, exact explanation is required, and the cases remain practical to maintain directly.

pairs.label: Consider ML
pairs.detail: Use ML when representative examples reveal a repeatable signal, error can be measured, and better predictions create enough value to fund ongoing operation.
pairs.explanation: Use ML when representative examples reveal a repeatable signal, error can be measured, and better predictions create enough value to fund ongoing operation.

pairs.label: Stop and reframe
pairs.detail: Do not proceed without a measurable target, an actionable output, representative evidence, a baseline, and a plan for high-cost mistakes.
pairs.explanation: Do not proceed without a measurable target, an actionable output, representative evidence, a baseline, and a plan for high-cost mistakes.

pairs.label: Behavior has multiple versions
pairs.detail: Code, feature definitions, training data, model artifacts, and thresholds must remain compatible.
pairs.explanation: Code, feature definitions, training data, model artifacts, and thresholds must remain compatible. A rollback restores the complete working set.

pairs.label: Tests become statistical
pairs.detail: Unit and integration tests still matter, but learned behavior also needs protected holdouts, confidence ranges, slice analysis, and invariant checks.
pairs.explanation: Unit and integration tests still matter, but learned behavior also needs protected holdouts, confidence ranges, slice analysis, and invariant checks.

pairs.label: Predictions create feedback
pairs.detail: Model decisions influence which items users see and which labels arrive later.
pairs.explanation: Model decisions influence which items users see and which labels arrive later. Exposure and selection bias can reinforce the current policy.

pairs.label: Quality shares the budget
pairs.detail: A useful model must also satisfy latency, throughput, cost, privacy, fairness, reliability, and maintainability constraints.
pairs.explanation: A useful model must also satisfy latency, throughput, cost, privacy, fairness, reliability, and maintainability constraints.
